public_rationale: The statement, from 28 April 2026, is about a hypothetical: AI data centers that 'somehow succeed' with consistent payments and tenancy. It caps their margins at '70% at best' but does not say which margin is meant, such as gross, EBITDA, operating or project-level. It names no operator and no period. It uses value words ('pathetic,' 'mediocre') and hedges the obsolescence point with 'might be difficult.' The evidence packet contains no evidence items. Testing the claim would mean choosing a margin type, an operator and a period that he did not give, and the result would depend on that choice. So the claim cannot be graded as written.
limitations: The packet contains no evidence on project-level economics for fully tenanted AI data centers.
No evidence on depreciation schedules or break-even timing was gathered.
A narrower, fully specified version of the claim might be testable against data that is not public.

criteria.support_condition: Not testable as written. A test would need a defined margin measure for successful, fully tenanted AI data centers showing at most 70%, plus evidence that break-even takes about six years of depreciation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not testable as written. A test would need evidence that successful, fully tenanted AI data centers reliably earn well above 70% on the measure he meant, or break even well before six years.
